nodes.title: Round 8 Play follow-up A: home play folds LIVE. When a level ends with no lessonId, /api/play/act signs the homeToken and, in the same request, folds it: server/play/home.js homeKtEvents verifies the token (this child's, a home token, row weight GAME or CHANCE only) and builds ONE event per level and skill with the learner's own mapping (server/learner/kt/home.js homePlayEvent: trail.solved -> won, trail.misses, trail.hints (0), trail.mal kit ids -> misconception, chance from the signed row weight, IST learning day, ids 'home:<child>:<day>:<level>:<n>'). The write is the out-of-turn writers' contract (fuseEvidence + writer.ledgerStmts + projection + facet rows in one transaction under the child lock, legal-mode guard and seq guard; idempotent by event id). No home table and no migration: the levels already folded that day are read back from kt_evidence by the home session id. TAXILA_HOME_PLAY_FOLD is ON unless set off/0/false/no. Cap choice: HOME_DAILY_CAP 3 -> 24 and it is a row-volume bound only; the knowledge rule is the ledger's HOME_DAY_LOG_CAP (+-ln 3 per skill per day, one learning step, never unaided, never the delayed check). At 3 the play cap bound first (two clean wins already saturate +ln 3; chance-weight wins take ~5) and kept a later miss from reaching the ledger's running clamp, which changed the ledger's rule. Test: 30 clean first-try home levels of one skill in one IST day never make it learned/mastered/unaided. Reverse if: the learner session changes HOME_DAY_LOG_CAP or the home weight (re-check the volume bound against the new saturation), a durable home record is wanted (then a migration, not kt_evidence read-back), or the /act write's latency shows on the play path (move the write after the response).

Round 8 Play follow-up B: a later level may switch FAMILY at most once a session, only when the session focus changes (the level just played showed a mal-rule mapped to a different kit misconception) to a mix-up another coverage entry admitting the skill tells apart better: the same chooseEntry score with novelty off, by its MARGIN 0.1, and the new entry's garam level must discriminate the focus (server/play/levels.js switchAfter, called from afterLevelBody; nextBody applies it and records `switched: { from, n }` in the signed body). The level carries a because { choice 'switch to <family>/<mode>', fact = the kit's belief text, source 'play_grade', kind 'play.switch' }. /api/play/next returns the new family's world and `switched`; the client (PlaySession) swaps the world, drops the old engine's story wrapper, and PlayStage remounts instead of re-levelling a different 3D engine (stageEngineRef). Real case today: kila/lcm 'product' (common-product) -> todo-jodo/atoms, for the seeds where kila's next level does not tell it apart. Reverse if: children switching mid-session lose the thread (watch abandon after a switch), or more than one switch a session is wanted (lift the once rule with a cooldown).

Round 8 Play follow-up C: a DELIBERATE Director fade beats the history fade. The request marks it `fadeFrom: "director"` (server/play/choose.js fadeFor); the because then says so { choice 'fade N', fact 'the lesson asked for fade N', source 'director', kind 'play.fade_director' } whenever her history would have said otherwise. /api/play/start honours fadeFrom only inside a lesson (from the home it would be a device claim); server/forge3/live.js buildLive marks m.fade as the Director's. No caller passes m.fade yet (Studio's seam calls buildLive without one): until then every lesson fade is the history's. Reverse if: the Director's fades prove worse than the history's for the same child (compare first-try rates by fade source).

Round 8 Play follow-up D: a non-clean level (not solved clean on the first decisive move) after a lift steps the lifted band back DOWN one step (lift - 1, never below 0, the unlifted band = her own pL), symmetric with the step up, with a because { choice 'next level a step easier', kind 'play.step_down', source 'play_grade' }. A mal-rule miss after a lift does both: that belief next AND one step easier ('next level tests that mix-up, a step easier'). An ungraded level steps nothing. Reverse if: the up/down oscillation shows (alternating win/miss bouncing the band each level: add hysteresis, e.g. two non-clean levels to step down).

Round 8 Play H: the child's 'why this game' line. Display text only, never a grade, no model: server/play/why.js whyLine(because, ctx) picks a shape by seed for the level's because when it is a mix-up focus (play.pick_mixup / play.mixup_focus), a step up, a step down or a family switch (never a fade, novelty, fit or studio_gate choice). {look} is a neutral noun phrase (data/play/engine-words.json look.<family>.<malRule>, else look.<family>), from the topic, never the belief. 'Last time' forms only when the because is from an earlier session (kind pick_mixup with when 'earlier': an open kt_misconception); this lesson or the level just played use forms with no time word. Spoken once per session per reason (session body whySaid; the client also never speaks while the lesson's teacher speaks: taxila:teacher-speaking). Grammar: hi/hinglish {look} is followed at once by a postposition; en {look} follows a preposition and look phrases carry their own article or are plural. Reverse if: children read it as a verdict (watch for 'galti' talk back), or the second line in the 360 px rail costs the world too much height (move it to the caption slot).

Round 8 Play item I: when Studio (C1) refuses a Studio v2 world at 360 px and offers the play family instead (buildLive reason 'phone'), the play session's because list carries { choice '<family>/<mode> for the phone', fact 'the Studio world is too small to play at 360 px', source 'studio_gate', kind 'play.studio_gate' } beside any picker because; it is not a child why-line kind. Reverse if: Studio's v2 worlds fit 360 px (the record would then never be true).

OPEN: play difficulty is not calibrated across families. Each level's proof.pFirstTry is the family generator's own estimate (solver-derived), so 'band garam 0.75' in kila and in todo-jodo are not the same difficulty, and the P1 fit term and the P2 lift/step-down compare uncalibrated numbers when they cross families (most visibly at a family switch). A calibration needs measured first-try outcomes per family x band: for a +-0.1 95% CI on a first-try rate near p = 0.7, n = z^2 p(1-p) / h^2 = 1.96^2 x 0.21 / 0.01 = 81 first-try outcomes per family x band; with children contributing several levels each (cluster m ~ 5, intra-child correlation rho ~ 0.2) the design effect 1 + (m-1) rho = 1.8 makes it ~146 per cell, i.e. ~30 families x 3 bands x 146 = ~13k levels. Re-fit: a 1PL (Rasch) model P(first try) = sigmoid(theta_child - b_level) with b_level = b_family,mode + beta_fade x fade + beta . level features (the generator's own difficulty knobs), child ability as a random effect (seeded from the ledger pL); then replace proof.pFirstTry by the fitted probability at the median child of the band and re-check the picker's BAND targets. Until then no cross-family difficulty claim is made to a parent.
